AGENT WORKFLOWSIndependent demo · 2026

RelayDesk.

Automation, with a handoff.

An independent portfolio demo exploring how an agent can prepare support decisions while a person retains control over sensitive actions.

Role
Product, full-stack & agent workflow development
Built with
LangGraph · PostgreSQL · FastAPI · Next.js
Source
github.com/KaitoA1008/relaydesk

The problem

What needed to work.

Turn a support request into a traceable decision without letting an automated recommendation silently become a real-world action.

The workflow

A deliberate path.

  1. Retrieve

    Check order ownership, find versioned policy passages and run read tools.

  2. Review

    Prepare a grounded reply and pause before any change for human approval.

  3. Resolve

    Execute the approved sandbox action, record its receipt and resolution history.

My contribution

Under the interface.

  • LangGraph routing with conditional edges and PostgreSQL checkpoints.
  • Read and write tools with before/after previews and re-checked preconditions.
  • Hybrid retrieval with optional local embeddings and a semantic intent fallback.
  • A 90-case benchmark, human approval, receipts and case history.

Engineering decisions

A deliberate approval boundary

The agent pauses before the reviewer approves an action.

Policy versions matter

The case retains the policy context used to prepare the decision.

Project context

Independent demonstration using synthetic support cases. On 90 hand-written cases, a local semantic fallback raises correct held-out outcomes from 18/30 to 25/30; 3 of 10 injection phrasings are still answered, but cannot run a tool without approval. Responses default to local templates; actions are sandboxed. No real refund, outbound email or customer-system integration is claimed.
